definition: Conciliatory means intended to soothe someone's anger and bring a dispute to an end — describing a tone, gesture, or statement that reaches out to make peace.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word conciliatory. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know conciliatory should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After the product recall sparked furious reviews, the CEO sent a conciliatory email admitting the mistake and promising free replacements to every customer.
Polite is weaker: a polite reply is merely courteous, while a conciliatory one actively works to cool anger and end the dispute.
Groveling is stronger: a conciliatory speaker offers peace while keeping some dignity, but a groveling one abandons every position and simply begs forgiveness.

Placating means quieting one particular person's anger in the moment, often by giving them whatever stops the shouting. A conciliatory move looks past the moment: it reaches out to settle the dispute itself, and it can come from either side of a two-way quarrel, dignity intact.

Peacemaking is working to end a conflict between other people — a mediator's or a diplomat's role, standing outside the fight. A conciliatory word or gesture comes from inside the quarrel: one of the parties itself extends the olive branch.

Appeasing means buying calm by handing an angry party what it demands, and the word hints the yielding goes too far. A conciliatory offer seeks peace without caving in — it cools anger while keeping the offerer's own position and dignity.

Conciliatory means intended to soothe someone's anger and bring a dispute to an end — describing a tone, gesture, or statement that reaches out to make peace.
On the second night of the bunk feud, the camp counselor gave a conciliatory talk, praising both sides' loyalty to their friends and proposing a shared campfire to clear the air.

The counselor's words are aimed squarely at cooling tempers and ending the conflict — crediting both sides and offering a peace gesture — which is what makes the talk conciliatory rather than merely friendly.

Conciliatory is not generic friendliness: it specifically describes a tone, gesture, or statement aimed at cooling someone's anger and ending a dispute — a conciliatory letter, offer, or handshake.
The related verb, reconcile (taught elsewhere in this unit), names the broader act of restoring harmony; conciliatory describes the peace-seeking manner of one particular message or move.

So reporters expected more of the same when the union chief stepped to the microphone on Friday afternoon.
Instead she struck a conciliatory note.
She admitted the walkout had hurt riders, praised the city's negotiators as honest people, and proposed returning to the table that weekend.
She surrendered nothing: the pay demand stood, she said plainly, and the safety grievances stood with it.
